description: COLOUR IDENTITY -- categorical colour as a MINTED, MDL-GATED SIGN over the opponent-colour VALUE. Builds DIRECTLY on colour-salience: salience answered WHERE to look (surround-relative opponent CONTRAST); this rung answers WHAT COLOUR IT IS (a categorical SIGN for the colour VALUE, downstream of salience). It instantiates the sd loop's DYNAMIC-QUANTIZATION pattern (decode -> recognize -> mint -> re-decode on codebook_epoch growth) for the 2-D integer opponent-colour subspace, with NO new Rust: ci_opponent computes the integer opponent coordinate (crg=cL-cM, cby=cS-(cL+cM)); ci_mint_category MINTS a ColourCategory quantum where a colour value CLUSTERS and MDL COMPRESSES (Count(same exact colour) >= 3 = m_min, which FALLS OUT of d=2: a category pays iff m*d > d+m <=> m > d/(d-1) = 2, so m>=3 -- no magic number); ci_assign writes each region's SIGN = its NEAREST minted quantum (Argmin by opponent Sqrt-distance) and re-decodes on codebook growth. So a scene with a few colour clusters mints ~that-many category quanta (k << N, MDL down), a seen colour is RECOGNIZED not re-minted (the has-guard), and a smooth gradient / iid noise mints ZERO (a category is minted ONLY if it compresses). Categories emerge from the colour distribution via MDL -- they are NOT hand-set (Witzel & Gegenfurtner). In-frame colour coordinate is INTEGER; the continuous lives ONLY in the cross-frame assignment distance (the frame/continuum invariant). NOT object colour re-ID / constancy / the 'what' layer -- that needs a bound object (the objecthood wall), the named frontier, out of scope. Reuses Count/Filter/NodesOfType/Argmin/Exists/Sqrt/Minus/Times/Plus/Gte + run_rules. Flag-gated on ColourIdentityParams.identity, OFF by default (§9). See VISION_COLOUR_IDENTITY_PREREG.md. v1.1.0 adds the ACHROMATOPSIA LESION flag (ColourIdentityParams.achromatopsia, OFF by default = INTACT): when armed it suppresses ONLY ci_mint_category + ci_assign (the categorical colour SIGN / naming), leaving ci_opponent (the chromatic SIGNAL) and the whole vision_colour salience seed (chromatic contrast / border / shape-from-colour) intact -- the colour-STRUCTURE / colour-SIGN dissociation of cerebral achromatopsia (Heywood & Cowey 1997). Default 0 => byte-identical to v1.0.0. See VISION_ACHROMATOPSIA_PREREG.md. v1.2.0 adds the REFUSAL BOUND (ColourIdentityParams.bound, OFF by default): L1b's uniqueness audit (VISION_UNIQUENESS_RESULTS.md) found ci_assign to be the worst case in its table -- an Argmin with ZERO Lte, no admission bound at all, so a probe at opponent distance 269.52 is confidently assigned and the equidistant probe is decided by a margin of exactly 0.0000; it cannot refuse, ever. When armed, ci_assign admits only INSIDE the minted codebook's PACKING RADIUS (r_i = 1/2 min_{j!=i} ||c_i-c_j||, the largest radius at which the codebook's own quanta do not overlap: 2r <= D), and the new ci_refuse rule fires on the exact complement, writing ci_refused instead of a sign. The bound FALLS OUT of the codebook (§13) -- a function of the minted prototypes, not a literal (7.8102 on a 3-category codebook, 10.0 on a 2-category one, neither chosen), reusing the distance ci_assign already computes; rival derivations (exact cluster extent = 0, the lattice step 1.0, an MDL radius from m_min/d) were audited and rejected ON MEASUREMENT. Absence-tolerant at k=1 by construction (Not(Exists) over an empty codebook-complement is true), where the packing radius is undefined and the bound is honestly VACUOUS. Default 0 => byte-identical to v1.1.0. See VISION_COLOUR_BOUND_PREREG.md. v1.3.0 FLIPS THAT DEFAULT: bound now ships ARMED (1.0). The k=1 rung (VISION_COLOUR_BOUND_K1_PREREG.md) asked whether a k=1 bound FALLS OUT and measured that NONE DOES -- and, more strongly, that none CAN: the packing radius is NON-INCREASING under codebook growth (a min over a superset cannot increase), so the k=1 radius upper-bounds every radius reachable by growth, and that supremum is UNBOUNDED. r(k=1) = +inf (admit everything) is this derivation's own limit, NOT a missing piece. Five rivals were audited and rejected, three ON MEASUREMENT: the mint's cluster extent (identically 0 -- exact-value minting gives a quantum ZERO intrinsic extent, so every length scale in this seed lives BETWEEN prototypes and at k=1 there is no between); the sqrt(2)/2 observational-resolution floor (indistinguishable from 0 on an integer lattice -- 100/100 observed coordinates integral); the lattice step 1.0 (regresses, injected and measured by the previous rung); the scene's measured dynamic range (0.0 in BOTH landed k=1 scenes, and NON-LOCAL -- the same observation against the same codebook flips verdict when an UNRELATED patch is added elsewhere); and observed-separation, the ONLY rival CONSISTENT with the landed bound (0 disagreements at k>=2) and UNDEFINED at k=1. The crux: the rivals DEFINED at k=1 are INCONSISTENT with the landed bound; the one that is CONSISTENT is UNDEFINED. CAVEAT, EXPLICIT AND NOT IMPLIED AWAY: arming the bound guarantees refusal for k>=2 ONLY. A single-quantum codebook still admits any colour at any distance (correct VQ semantics: a lone quantum owns all of space). The flip is a STRICT improvement -- measured DELTA-ON EMPTY across all five landed scenes and the k=1 regime byte-identical ON vs OFF -- never a total guarantee. Closing the k=1 regime needs a mint with INTRINSIC EXTENT, i.e. colour identity's own NAMED FRONTIER (perceptual NEARNESS in minting). See VISION_COLOUR_BOUND_K1_PREREG.md.

microtheory.label: colour identity: categorical colour as an MDL-gated quantum minted from the opponent-colour value subspace

rules.name: ci_opponent
rules.comment: Compute the in-frame INTEGER opponent coordinate of a cell from its raw cone attrs: crg = cL-cM (red-green), cby = cS-(cL+cM) (blue-yellow), the two chromatic opponent axes orthogonal to luminance -- the SAME axes the colour-salience rung used, but here the VALUE (identity), not the surround-relative contrast (salience). Reads ONLY self raw cones so firing order is irrelevant. The coordinate is INTEGER (the frame/continuum invariant: in-frame is the integer lattice; the continuous appears only in the cross-frame distance ci_assign uses). Flag-gated on ColourIdentityParams.identity>0.5, OFF by default (§9). Once (op_done).

rules.name: ci_mint_category
rules.comment: DYNAMIC QUANTIZATION (the sd loop's sd_mint_quantum pattern for the colour subspace): MINT a ColourCategory quantum at an exact opponent colour value where the value CLUSTERS and MDL COMPRESSES. Gates: (1) identity>0.5; (2) the opponent field is complete (Not Exists Region with op_done<0.5) so the member count is exact, never a transient undercount; (3) THE MDL GATE -- Count(Filter(Region, same exact crg&cby)) >= 3: this colour recurs >= m_min times. m_min=3 FALLS OUT of the coordinate dimensionality d=2 (§13, NOT tuned): a category costs a d-integer prototype and saves 1 label per member vs a d-integer raw coord, so it pays iff m*d > d+m, i.e. m > d/(d-1); for d=2 that is m>2 <=> m>=3 (at m=2: raw 4 vs categorized 2+2=4, equal, refuse); (4) the CANONICAL-REPRESENTATIVE guard -- only the top-left (lexicographic (rrow,rcol)) region of a colour may mint, so under s.tick()'s batch application (all bindings snapshotted before any effect) exactly ONE region per DISTINCT colour passes and mints exactly ONE category per colour (picking a canonical member, the ground rung's 'single unified rule' lesson -- NOT a magic threshold); (5) Not(Exists ColourCategory at this colour) -- recognize-not-re-mint across passes / re-presentations (a seen colour is never re-minted). Effects: add the ColourCategory{crg,cby,members,minted:1}, link it has_category from the scene, and bump Scene.epoch (the codebook_epoch re-arm so ci_assign re-decodes on growth). Flag-gated on identity>0.5, OFF by default (§9).

rules.name: ci_assign
rules.comment: DEQUANTIZATION (the sd loop's decode/recognize pattern): a region's categorical colour SIGN is its NEAREST minted ColourCategory quantum -- Argmin over ColourCategory by the cross-frame opponent distance dist(R,c)=Sqrt((R.crg-c.crg)^2+(R.cby-c.cby)^2) (the ONLY continuous quantity, living in the cross-frame comparison, never in a frame's coordinate -- the frame/continuum invariant). Writes sign_rg/sign_by (the assigned quantum's coordinate) and sign_dist (the residual to it). A cell whose colour EXACTLY equals a prototype gets sign_dist=0 and that category's sign (recognize); an off-prototype cell gets its nearest quantum. Re-decodes on codebook growth: gated on assigned_epoch != Scene.epoch (the sd_redecode re-arm), so every sign reflects the FINAL codebook once minting settles. Gated on Count(ColourCategory)>0 so it never fires before any quantum exists. Flag-gated on identity>0.5, OFF by default (§9).

rules.name: ci_refuse
rules.comment: THE REFUSAL (VISION_COLOUR_BOUND_PREREG.md): a region whose nearest minted quantum lies OUTSIDE that quantum's PACKING RADIUS gets NO categorical sign. The packing radius r_i = 1/2 min_{j!=i} ||c_i-c_j|| is the largest radius at which the codebook's own quanta do not overlap; two balls of radius r around prototypes separated by D are disjoint iff 2r <= D, so admission is 2*dist(R,winner) <= min_{c!=winner} dist(winner,c) and this rule fires on its exact complement. The bound FALLS OUT of the codebook (§13): it is a function of the minted prototypes, not a literal -- 7.8102 on a 3-category codebook, 10.0 on a 2-category one, neither chosen -- and it reuses the very distance ci_assign already computes, applied prototype-to-prototype. Expressed as Not(Exists other prototype closer than 2*residual), so the k=1 case (no other prototype; packing radius undefined) is absence-tolerant BY CONSTRUCTION and admits -- the honest residual: the bound is vacuous at k=1. Writes ONLY new attrs (ci_refused, ci_refused_dist) and never clears sign_*, so a refused region keeps sign_dist=-1.0 (the refused readout) and every effect value is constant once set (run_rules terminates on exact value equality). Sets assigned_epoch so it fires once per epoch and re-arms with ci_assign on codebook growth. Flag-gated on ColourIdentityParams.bound>0.5, OFF by default (§9) -- at the default this rule can never fire.
